script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. PARK - DAY

BEN, in his late 30s, a charming but disheveled man, sits on a bench, lost in thought. A WOMAN, JENNY, in her mid-30s, passes by, noticing Ben's sad expression.

JENNY: (smiling) Hi there. Long day?

BEN: (surprised) Huh? Oh, no. Just... thinking.

JENNY: (sitting down next to him) Well, if you ever need someone to talk to, I'm here.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Ben and Jenny sit across from each other, sipping their coffees.

BEN: I can't believe it's been a year already.

JENNY: (nods) I know. It's amazing how time flies.

BEN: (sighs) I still can't believe I missed that plane.

JENNY: (smiling) You know, life has a funny way of working things out.

BEN: (looks up) Really?

JENNY: (yes nod) Yes. Like how you ended up meeting me today.

INT. BEN'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Ben is packing a bag, looking distraught. Jenny enters.

JENNY: Ben, what's going on?

BEN: (sad) I've made a huge mistake. I have to leave.

JENNY: (concerned) What mistake? Where are you going?

BEN: (hesitates) I can't tell you. But I have to make things right.

JENNY: (angry) And just like that, you're leaving me again?

BEN: (apologetic) I'm so sorry, Jenny. I never meant for things to turn out like this.

INT. COURTROOM - DAY

Ben stands trial for embezzling money from his former employer. Jenny testifies on his behalf, speaking of his good character.

JENNY: (on the stand) Ben is a kind and honest man. He would never intentionally steal. He made a mistake, but he's made amends.

INT. PRISON VISITATION ROOM - DAY

Ben sits across from an older man, MIKE, his former boss.

MIKE: (angry) You betrayed me, Ben. I trusted you.

BEN: (apologetic) I know, Mike. I'm truly sorry. I was in a tough spot, and I made a terrible decision.

MIKE: (sighs) And now you have to pay the price.

BEN: (nods) Yes, I do. But I've learned from this experience. I've learned to be more responsible and to think before I act.

MIKE: (pauses) I can't forgive you easily, Ben. But I can see the change in you. I'll think about it.

INT. PRISON YARD - DAY

Ben is playing a game of pick-up soccer with other inmates. Jenny arrives, wearing a prison volunteer uniform. She approaches Ben.

JENNY: (smiling) I brought you a ball.

BEN: (surprised) Jenny? What are you doing here?

JENNY: (grinning) I wanted to see you. And maybe help out a little.

BEN: (relieved) That means a lot, Jenny. Thank you.

EXT. PRISON GROUNDS - NIGHT

As Ben walks back to his cell, he notices MIKE, now sitting on a bench, watching the sunset.

MIKE: (calling out) Ben!

Ben approaches.

MIKE: (looking at Ben) I've been thinking... I can forgive you. You've paid your debt to society. Now, it's time for you to start living your life again.

BEN: (grateful) Thank you, Mike. I won't let you down.

FADE OUT.

THE END
